macros.name: datatoolasciiend
macros.doc: Does nothing but influences sorting.

macros.name: datatoolasciistart
macros.doc: Does nothing but influences sorting.

macros.name: datatoolctrlboundary
macros.doc: Does nothing but influences sorting.

macros.name: DataToolDateFmt
macros.doc: Formats the date.

macros.name: DataToolDateTimeFmt
macros.doc: Use to format timestamps (datetime date types).

macros.name: datatoolparen
macros.doc: This command normally expands to \space (⟨text⟩).

macros.name: datatoolparenstart
macros.doc: Designed to indicate the start of parenthetical content, this command expands to \space normally.

macros.name: datatoolpersoncomma
macros.doc: Designed to indicate word inversion for a person, this command expands to ,\space normally.

macros.name: datatoolplacecomma
macros.doc: Designed to indicate a comma to clarify a place, this command expands to ,\space normally.

macros.name: datatoolSetCurrencySort
macros.doc: Locally redefines common currency commands to their string alternatives.

macros.name: datatoolsubjectcomma
macros.doc: Designed to indicate heading inversion (subjects, concepts and objects), this command expands to ,\space normally.

macros.name: DataToolTimeFmt
macros.doc: Formats the time.

macros.name: DataToolTimeStampFmtSep
macros.doc: This is placed between the date and time.

macros.name: DataToolTimeStampNoZoneFmt
macros.doc: Formats the date and time.

macros.name: DataToolTimeStampWithZoneFmt
macros.doc: Formats the date, time and time zone.

macros.name: DataToolTimeZoneFmt
macros.doc: Formats the time zone offset.

macros.name: dtlabs
macros.doc: Defines ⟨cs⟩ to the absolute value of ⟨num⟩.

macros.name: dtladd
macros.doc: Calculates ⟨num1⟩ + ⟨num2⟩ (addition) and stores the result in the control sequence ⟨cs⟩, where the numbers are plain numbers.

macros.name: DTLadd
macros.doc: Calculates ⟨num1⟩ + ⟨num2⟩ and stores the result in the control sequence ⟨cs⟩, where the numbers are formatted numbers.

macros.name: dtladdall
macros.doc: Defines ⟨cs⟩ to the sum of all the values in the comma-separated list of numbers.

macros.name: DTLaddall
macros.doc: Sums all the values in ⟨num list⟩ and stores in ⟨cmd⟩ which must be a control sequence.

macros.name: DTLafterinitials
macros.doc: Defines what to do after the final initial.

macros.name: DTLaposinitialpunc
macros.doc: This command is used to encapsulate an initial in a word split by an apostrophe in the form ⟨head⟩'⟨tail⟩.

macros.name: DTLassignlettergroup
macros.doc: Obtains the letter group from the sort value.

macros.name: DTLbetweeninitials
macros.doc: Defines what to do between initials.

macros.name: dtlbreak
macros.doc: Break out of loop at the end of current iteration.

macros.name: dtlclip
macros.doc: Removes redundant trailing zeros from ⟨num⟩ and stores the result in ⟨cs⟩.

macros.name: DTLclip
macros.doc: Converts the formatted number to a plain number, clips it using \dtlclip and stores the result as a formatted number in the control sequence ⟨cs⟩.

macros.name: dtlcompare
macros.doc: Compares ⟨string1⟩ and ⟨string2⟩, and stores the result in the count register ⟨count⟩.

macros.name: DTLconverttodecimal
macros.doc: Converts a formatted number ⟨num⟩ to a plain number and stores the result in ⟨cs⟩.

macros.name: DTLcurr
macros.doc: This command will expand to \DTLcurr⟨ISO⟩, if defined, otherwise it will expand to ⟨ISO⟩.

macros.name: DTLcurrChar
macros.doc: Expands to the currency character associated with the currency identified by ⟨ISO⟩, or nothing if not defined.

macros.name: DTLcurrCodeOrSymOrChar
macros.doc: This is used in both \DTLcurr⟨ISO⟩ and \dtlcurrfmtsep and should be defined to expand to one of its arguments (ignoring the other two). The default is to expand to ⟨symbol⟩.

macros.name: DTLcurrency
macros.doc: Formats ⟨value⟩ as a currency using \DTLfmtcurrency with the default currency symbol.

macros.name: DTLCurrencySymbol
macros.doc: Expands to the internal command used to store the default currency symbol.

macros.name: DTLCurrentLocaleGetInitialLetter
macros.doc: This is used by \DTLGetInitialLetter and \DTLassignlettergroup to obtain the initial letter of the given text.

macros.name: dtlcurrfmtsep
macros.doc: Separator used by currency formats.

macros.name: DTLcurrStr
macros.doc: Expands to the detokenised string value associated with currency ⟨ISO⟩ or to nothing if not defined.

macros.name: DTLcurrXXX
macros.doc: Generic currency XXX with symbol ¤.

macros.name: DTLdatumcurrency
macros.doc: Expands to the currency symbol if the parsed value was a currency, otherwise expands to empty.

macros.name: DTLdatumtoDTM
macros.doc: Converts the time stamp stored in the given datum command to a datetime2 date saved with \DTMsavetimestamp, \DTMsavedate, or \DTLsavetime.

macros.name: DTLdatumtype
macros.doc: Expands to an integer representing the data type: 0 (string), 1 (integer), 2 (decimal), 3 (currency), 4 (timestamp), 5 (date), 6 (time) or -1 (unknown).

macros.name: DTLdatumvalue
macros.doc: Expands to the numeric value (as a plain number) if the parsed value was numerical, otherwise expands to empty.

macros.name: DTLdecimaltocurrency
macros.doc: This converts a decimal number into the locale dependent currency format.

macros.name: DTLdecimaltocurrency
macros.doc: This converts a decimal number into the locale dependent currency format.

macros.name: DTLdecimaltodate
macros.doc: Define command to convert a number (a Julian Day Number) into a date datum.

macros.name: DTLdecimaltodatetime
macros.doc: Define command to convert a decimal number into a datetime datum.

macros.name: DTLdecimaltolocale
macros.doc: Converts a plain number ⟨num⟩ into a formatted number and stores the result in ⟨cs⟩.

macros.name: DTLdecimaltotime
macros.doc: Define command to convert a decimal number (Julian time of day fraction) into a time datum.

macros.name: DTLDefaultLocaleWordHandler
macros.doc: This uses \DTLCurrentLocaleWordHandler{⟨cs⟩} to convert ⟨cs⟩ to a byte sequence that ensures the locale’s alphabetic ordering, and then appends \datatoolctrlboundary to ⟨cs⟩.

macros.name: DTLdefcurrency
macros.doc: Defines a new currency with associated ISO code, symbol and string equivalent.

macros.name: DTLdefcurrency
macros.doc: Defines a new currency with associated ISO code, symbol and string equivalent.

macros.name: dtldiv
macros.doc: Divides two numbers and stores the result in ⟨cs⟩.

macros.name: DTLdiv
macros.doc: Converts the formatted numbers ⟨num1⟩ and ⟨num2⟩ to plain numbers and divides them (⟨num1⟩÷ ⟨num2⟩) using \dtldiv.

macros.name: dtlfallbackaction
macros.doc: If two sort values are identical, this command is used to determine whether or not the sort function should swap the elements.

macros.name: DTLfetchlistelement
macros.doc: Fetches the ⟨idx⟩th element in the list and stores in ⟨cs⟩.

macros.name: DTLfmtcurr
macros.doc: This will use the format associated with the given currency code.

macros.name: DTLfmtcurrency
macros.doc: Format currency using given symbol.

macros.name: DTLformatlist
macros.doc: Formats the comma-separated list supplied in its argument.

macros.name: DTLformatlist*
macros.doc: Formats the comma-separated list supplied in its argument.

macros.name: DTLgetDataTypeName
macros.doc: Expands to textual label associated with the data type ⟨number⟩.

macros.name: DTLGetInitialLetter
macros.doc: Obtains the first letter of ⟨text⟩ and stores it in the control sequence ⟨cs⟩.

macros.name: dtlicompare
macros.doc: Compares ⟨string1⟩ and ⟨string2⟩ and stores the result in the count register ⟨count-reg⟩, where 0 indicates the strings are the same, -1 means that ⟨string1⟩ comes before (less than) ⟨string2⟩ and 1 means that ⟨string1⟩ comes after (greater than) ⟨string2⟩ (case-insensitive) .

macros.name: DTLifAllLowerCase
macros.doc: Does ⟨true⟩ if ⟨string⟩ contains only lowercase characters (disregarding punctuation and spaces), otherwise does ⟨false⟩.

macros.name: DTLifAllUpperCase
macros.doc: Does ⟨true⟩ if ⟨string⟩ contains only uppercase characters (disregarding punctuation and spaces), otherwise does ⟨false⟩.

macros.name: DTLifcasedatatype
macros.doc: If ⟨arg⟩ is a string, do ⟨string case⟩, if ⟨arg⟩ is an integer do ⟨int case⟩, if ⟨arg⟩ is a real number, do ⟨real case⟩, if ⟨arg⟩ is currency, do ⟨currency case⟩.

macros.name: DTLifclosedbetween
macros.doc: Does \DTLifnumclosedbetween if {⟨arg⟩}, ⟨min⟩ and ⟨max⟩ are numerical, otherwise do \DTLifstringclosedbetween or \DTLifstringclosedbetween*.

macros.name: DTLifclosedbetween*
macros.doc: Does \DTLifnumclosedbetween if {⟨arg⟩}, ⟨min⟩ and ⟨max⟩ are numerical, otherwise do \DTLifstringclosedbetween or \DTLifstringclosedbetween*.

macros.name: DTLifcurrency
macros.doc: Tests the first argument, if it’s currency do second argument, otherwise do third argument.

macros.name: DTLifcurrencyunit
macros.doc: Parses ⟨arg⟩ and does ⟨true⟩ if ⟨arg⟩ is a recognised currency formatted number and uses the currency ⟨symbol⟩, otherwise it does ⟨false⟩ (see Example 15).

macros.name: DTLifdate
macros.doc: Tests the first argument, if it’s a date (no time) do second argument, otherwise do third argument.

macros.name: DTLifEndsWith
macros.doc: If ⟨string⟩ ends with ⟨substring⟩, this does ⟨true part⟩, otherwise it does ⟨false part⟩.

macros.name: DTLifEndsWith*
macros.doc: If ⟨string⟩ ends with ⟨substring⟩, this does ⟨true part⟩, otherwise it does ⟨false part⟩.

macros.name: DTLifeq
macros.doc: Does \DTLifnumeq if both ⟨arg1⟩ and ⟨arg2⟩ are numerical, otherwise do \DTLifstringeq or \DTLifstringeq*.

macros.name: DTLifeq*
macros.doc: Does \DTLifnumeq if both ⟨arg1⟩ and ⟨arg2⟩ are numerical, otherwise do \DTLifstringeq or \DTLifstringeq*.

macros.name: DTLifFPclosedbetween
macros.doc: Determines if ⟨min⟩ ≤ ⟨num⟩ ≤ ⟨max⟩.

macros.name: DTLifFPopenbetween
macros.doc: Determines if ⟨min⟩ < ⟨num⟩ < ⟨max⟩ where all arguments are in standard fixed point notation.

macros.name: DTLifgt
macros.doc: Does \DTLifnumgt if both ⟨arg1⟩ and ⟨arg2⟩ are numerical, otherwise do \DTLifstringgt or \DTLifstringgt*.

macros.name: DTLifgt*
macros.doc: Does \DTLifnumgt if both ⟨arg1⟩ and ⟨arg2⟩ are numerical, otherwise do \DTLifstringgt or \DTLifstringgt*.

macros.name: DTLifinlist
macros.doc: If ⟨element⟩ is contained in the comma-separated list given by ⟨list⟩, then do ⟨true part⟩ otherwise do false part.

macros.name: DTLifint
macros.doc: Tests the first argument, if it’s an integer do second argument, otherwise do third argument.

macros.name: dtlifnumclosedbetween
macros.doc: Does ⟨true⟩ if ⟨num⟩ lies between ⟨min⟩ and ⟨max⟩, including the end points (that is, ⟨min⟩ ≤ ⟨num⟩ ≤ ⟨max⟩) otherwise does ⟨false⟩.

macros.name: DTLifnumclosedbetween
macros.doc: Does ⟨true⟩ if ⟨num⟩ lies between ⟨min⟩ and ⟨max⟩, including the end points (that is, ⟨min⟩ ≤ ⟨num⟩ ≤ ⟨max⟩) otherwise does ⟨false⟩, where the values are formatted numbers.

macros.name: dtlifnumeq
macros.doc: Does ⟨true part⟩ if ⟨num1⟩=⟨num2⟩, otherwise does ⟨false part⟩.

macros.name: DTLifnumeq
macros.doc: Does ⟨true⟩ if ⟨num1⟩ equals ⟨num2⟩ (⟨num1⟩ = ⟨num2⟩) otherwise does ⟨false⟩, where the values are formatted numbers.

macros.name: DTLifnumerical
macros.doc: Tests the first argument, if it’s numerical do second argument, otherwise do third argument.

macros.name: dtlifnumgt
macros.doc: Does ⟨true⟩ if ⟨num1⟩ is greater than ⟨num2⟩ otherwise does ⟨false⟩.

macros.name: DTLifnumgt
macros.doc: Does ⟨true⟩ if ⟨num1⟩ is greater than ⟨num2⟩ (⟨num1⟩ > ⟨num2⟩) otherwise does ⟨false⟩, where the values are formatted numbers.

macros.name: dtlifnumlt
macros.doc: Does ⟨true⟩ if ⟨num1⟩ is less than ⟨num2⟩ otherwise does ⟨false⟩.

macros.name: DTLifnumlt
macros.doc: Does ⟨true⟩ if ⟨num1⟩ is less than ⟨num2⟩ (⟨num1⟩ < ⟨num2⟩) otherwise does ⟨false⟩, where the values are formatted numbers.

macros.name: dtlifnumopenbetween
macros.doc: Does ⟨true⟩ if ⟨num⟩ lies between ⟨min⟩ and ⟨max⟩, excluding the end points (that is, ⟨min⟩ < ⟨num⟩ < ⟨max⟩) otherwise does ⟨false⟩.

macros.name: DTLifnumopenbetween
macros.doc: Does ⟨true⟩ if ⟨num⟩ lies between ⟨min⟩ and ⟨max⟩, excluding the end points (that is, ⟨min⟩ < ⟨num⟩ < ⟨max⟩) otherwise does ⟨false⟩, where the values are formatted numbers.

macros.name: DTLifopenbetween
macros.doc: Does \DTLifnumopenbetween if {⟨arg⟩}, ⟨min⟩ and ⟨max⟩ are numerical, otherwise do \DTLifstringopenbetween or \DTLifstringopenbetween*.

macros.name: DTLifopenbetween*
macros.doc: Does \DTLifnumopenbetween if {⟨arg⟩}, ⟨min⟩ and ⟨max⟩ are numerical, otherwise do \DTLifstringopenbetween or \DTLifstringopenbetween*.

macros.name: DTLifreal
macros.doc: Tests the first argument, if it’s a real number (not an integer or currency) do second argument, otherwise do third argument.

macros.name: DTLifstring
macros.doc: Tests the first argument, if it’s a string do second argument, otherwise do third argument.

macros.name: DTLifstringclosedbetween
macros.doc: Does ⟨true⟩ if ⟨str⟩ is lexicographically between ⟨min⟩ and ⟨max⟩, inclusive.

macros.name: DTLifstringclosedbetween*
macros.doc: Does ⟨true⟩ if ⟨str⟩ is lexicographically between ⟨min⟩ and ⟨max⟩, inclusive.

macros.name: DTLifstringlt
macros.doc: \DTLifstringlt is a test if one string is lexicographical less than another.

macros.name: DTLifstringlt*
macros.doc: \DTLifstringlt is a test if one string is lexicographical less than another.

macros.name: DTLifstringopenbetween
macros.doc: Does ⟨true⟩ if ⟨str⟩ is lexicographically between ⟨min⟩ and ⟨max⟩, but is not equal to ⟨min⟩ or ⟨max⟩.

macros.name: DTLifstringopenbetween*
macros.doc: Does ⟨true⟩ if ⟨str⟩ is lexicographically between ⟨min⟩ and ⟨max⟩, but is not equal to ⟨min⟩ or ⟨max⟩.

macros.name: DTLifSubString
macros.doc: If ⟨sub string⟩ is contained in ⟨string⟩ does ⟨true part⟩, otherwise does ⟨false part⟩.

macros.name: DTLifSubString*
macros.doc: If ⟨sub string⟩ is contained in ⟨string⟩ does ⟨true part⟩, otherwise does ⟨false part⟩.

macros.name: DTLiftemporal
macros.doc: Tests the first argument, if it’s temporal do second argument, otherwise do third argument.

macros.name: DTLiftime
macros.doc: Tests the first argument, if it’s a time (no date) do second argument, otherwise do third argument.

macros.name: DTLinitialpunc
macros.doc: This command is used to encapsulate each initial (except in the case of a word containing an apostrophe) and the following period/full stop.

macros.name: DTLinitials
macros.doc: Splits ⟨text⟩ into words and displays the initial of each word.

macros.name: dtlinsertinto
macros.doc: Globally inserts ⟨element⟩ into a sorted list (provided in the definition of the command ⟨sorted-list cs⟩) according to the comparison macro ⟨criteria cs⟩, which should have the same syntax as that for \dtlsortlist.

macros.name: DTLisiPrefix
macros.doc: Tests if first argument starts with second argument.

macros.name: DTLisiSubString
macros.doc: Tests if second argument is contained in first argument (no case).

macros.name: DTLisiSuffix
macros.doc: Tests if first argument ends with second argument.

macros.name: DTLisPrefix
macros.doc: Tests if first argument starts with second argument.

macros.name: DTLisSubString
macros.doc: Tests if second argument is contained in first argument.

macros.name: DTLisSuffix
macros.doc: Tests if first argument ends with second argument.

macros.name: DTLlistelement
macros.doc: Does the ⟨idx⟩th element in the list.

macros.name: DTLlistformatitem
macros.doc: Formats an item within \DTLformatlist.

macros.name: DTLlistformatlastsep
macros.doc: Separator used between the final two elements in \DTLformatlist.

macros.name: dtlmax
macros.doc: Defines ⟨cs⟩ to the larger of the two numbers.

macros.name: DTLmax
macros.doc: Converts the formatted numbers ⟨num1⟩ and ⟨num2⟩ to plain numbers and determines the maximum.

macros.name: dtlmaxall
macros.doc: Defines ⟨cs⟩ to the maximum in the comma-separated list of numbers.

macros.name: DTLmaxall
macros.doc: Finds the maximum value in ⟨num list⟩ and stores in ⟨cmd⟩ which must be a control sequence.

macros.name: dtlmeanforall
macros.doc: Defines ⟨cs⟩ to the mean (average) of all the values in the comma-separated list of numbers.

macros.name: DTLmeanforall
macros.doc: Computes the arithmetic mean of all the values in ⟨num list⟩ and stores in ⟨cmd⟩ which must be a control sequence.

macros.name: dtlmin
macros.doc: Defines ⟨cs⟩ to the smaller of the two numbers.

macros.name: DTLmin
macros.doc: Converts the formatted numbers ⟨num1⟩ and ⟨num2⟩ to plain numbers and determines the minimum.

macros.name: dtlminall
macros.doc: Defines ⟨cs⟩ to the minimum in the comma-separated list of numbers.

macros.name: DTLminall
macros.doc: Finds the minimum value in ⟨num list⟩ and stores in ⟨cmd⟩ which must be a control sequence.

macros.name: dtlmul
macros.doc: Multiplies two numbers and stores the result in ⟨cs⟩.

macros.name: DTLmul
macros.doc: Converts the formatted numbers ⟨num1⟩ and ⟨num2⟩ to plain numbers and multiplies them (⟨num1⟩ × ⟨num2⟩).

macros.name: dtlneg
macros.doc: Defines ⟨cs⟩ to the negative of ⟨num⟩.

macros.name: DTLneg
macros.doc: Converts the formatted numbers ⟨num⟩ to a plain number and stores the negation (−⟨num⟩) as a formatted number in the command ⟨cs⟩.

macros.name: dtlnonlettergroup
macros.doc: By default, this simply expands to ⟨character⟩. A language file may redefine this to produce a textual title.

macros.name: DTLnumbernull
macros.doc: Represents null for values that are expected to be numeric.

macros.name: DTLnumcompare
macros.doc: Compares ⟨num1⟩ and ⟨num2⟩ numerically, where the arguments are formatted numbers or datum control sequences.

macros.name: DTLnumitemsinlist
macros.doc: Counts the number of elements in the list and defines the command ⟨cs⟩ to that number.

macros.name: dtlpadleadingzeros
macros.doc: Expands to a plain number that is the supplied ⟨value⟩ padded with leading zeros to the number of digits identified in the ⟨num-digits⟩ argument.

macros.name: dtlparsewords
macros.doc: Iterates through the given phrase. Hyphens are considered word boundaries.

macros.name: DTLPreProcessDateGroup
macros.doc: Hook to pre-process date group.

macros.name: DTLPreProcessNonLetterGroup
macros.doc: This hook is used for a non-letter and does nothing by default.

macros.name: DTLPreProcessTimeGroup
macros.doc: Hook to pre-process time group.

macros.name: DTLresetLanguage
macros.doc: Reset all language (not region) related commands.

macros.name: DTLresetRegion
macros.doc: Reset all region related commands.

macros.name: dtlround
macros.doc: Rounds ⟨num⟩ to ⟨dp⟩ decimal places and stores the result in the control sequence ⟨cs⟩, where the number is a plain number.

macros.name: DTLround
macros.doc: Sets ⟨cmd⟩ to ⟨num⟩ rounded to ⟨num digits⟩ digits after the decimal character.

macros.name: DTLscinum
macros.doc: If siunitx is loaded, this will be defined to use \num otherwise it will simply expand to its argument.

macros.name: dtlsdforall
macros.doc: Calculates the standard deviation of all the numbers in the comma-separated list ⟨num list⟩ and stores the result in the control sequence ⟨cs⟩, where the numbers are plain numbers.

macros.name: dtlsdforall
macros.doc: Calculates the standard deviation of all the numbers in the comma-separated list ⟨num list⟩ and stores the result in the control sequence ⟨cs⟩, where the numbers are plain numbers.

macros.name: DTLsdforall
macros.doc: Computes the standard deviation of all the values in ⟨num list⟩ and stores in ⟨cmd⟩ which must be a control sequence.

macros.name: DTLsetcurrencydatum
macros.doc: Defines the control sequence ⟨cs⟩ as a currency datum, where ⟨formatted value⟩ is the formatted currency and ⟨value⟩ is the currency value as a plain number.

macros.name: DTLsetdecimaldatum
macros.doc: Sets ⟨cs⟩ to a decimal datum.

macros.name: DTLsetdefaultcurrency
macros.doc: Sets the default currency.

macros.name: DTLsetfpdatum
macros.doc: Sets ⟨cs⟩ to a floating point datum.

macros.name: DTLsetintegerdatum
macros.doc: Sets ⟨cs⟩ to an integer datum.

macros.name: DTLsetLocaleOptions
macros.doc: User command for setting options for the given locale.

macros.name: DTLsetLocaleOptions
macros.doc: User command for setting options for the given locale.

macros.name: DTLsetLocaleOptions*
macros.doc: User command for setting options for the given locale.

macros.name: DTLsetLocaleOptions*
macros.doc: User command for setting options for the given locale.

macros.name: DTLsetnumberchars
macros.doc: Sets the current number group character and decimal character.

macros.name: DTLsetstringdatum
macros.doc: Sets ⟨cs⟩ to a string datum.

macros.name: DTLsettemporaldatum
macros.doc: Sets ⟨cs⟩ to a date/time datum.

macros.name: DTLsetup
macros.doc: Provide user interface command to set options later.

macros.name: DTLshufflelist
macros.doc: Shuffle a comma-separated list.

macros.name: DTLsortedactual
macros.doc: Expands to the actual element.

macros.name: DTLsortedvalue
macros.doc: Expands to the string sort value.

macros.name: DTLsortlettercasehandler
macros.doc: A case-sensitive letter order handler.

macros.name: DTLsortletterhandler
macros.doc: A case-insensitive letter order handler.

macros.name: dtlsortlist
macros.doc: Sorts the given comma-separated list according to the ⟨criteria⟩ command, which must take three arguments.

macros.name: DTLsortwordcasehandler
macros.doc: A case-sensitive word order handler.

macros.name: DTLsortwordhandler
macros.doc: A case-insensitive word order handler.

macros.name: DTLsplitstring
macros.doc: Splits ⟨string⟩ at ⟨split text⟩ and defines ⟨before cmd⟩ to the pre-split text and ⟨after cmd⟩ to the post-split text.

macros.name: dtlsqrt
macros.doc: Square root number and store the result in ⟨cs⟩.

macros.name: DTLstoreinitials
macros.doc: Splits ⟨text⟩ into words and stores the initial of each word in the control sequence ⟨cs⟩.

macros.name: DTLstringnull
macros.doc: Represents null for values that are expected to be strings.

macros.name: dtlsub
macros.doc: Subtracts two numbers and stores the result in ⟨cs⟩.

macros.name: DTLsub
macros.doc: Converts the formatted numbers ⟨num1⟩ and ⟨num2⟩ to plain numbers and subtracts ⟨num2⟩ from ⟨num1⟩ (⟨num1⟩ − ⟨num2⟩).

macros.name: DTLsubstitute
macros.doc: Substitutes the first occurrence of ⟨original⟩ with ⟨replacement⟩ within the expansion text of the command ⟨cs⟩.

macros.name: DTLtemporalvalue
macros.doc: This simply expands to the first argument by default, which is the numeric value associated with the data.

macros.name: dtltexorsort
macros.doc: This normally expands to just its first argument but inside \DTLsortwordlist it expands to its second argument instead.

macros.name: dtltrunc
macros.doc: Truncates ⟨num⟩ to ⟨dp⟩ decimal places and stores the result in ⟨cs⟩.

macros.name: DTLtrunc
macros.doc: Sets ⟨cmd⟩ to ⟨num⟩ truncated to ⟨num digits⟩ digits after the decimal character.

macros.name: DTLusedatum
macros.doc: Expands to the original value ⟨content⟩ that was parsed (or the expanded value in the case of \DTLxparse, or the reformatted string value, if the applicable option was in effect).

macros.name: dtlvarianceforall
macros.doc: Defines ⟨cs⟩ to the variance of all the values in the comma-separated list of numbers.

macros.name: dtlvarianceforall
macros.doc: Defines ⟨cs⟩ to the variance of all the values in the comma-separated list of numbers.

macros.name: DTLvarianceforall
macros.doc: Computes the variance of all the values in ⟨num list⟩ and stores in ⟨cmd⟩ which must be a control sequence.

macros.name: edtlinsertinto
macros.doc: First expands ⟨element⟩ before inserting into the list.
